ask: Draft the one-home rule: the builder.md wording, how a variant extends a shared piece in CSS, Swift and tests, and the compliance-check group that finds copies. Use the q_max map-skill drift as the worked example.
note: Already planned in parts: design tokens in one file generated into CSS and Swift (o2, r2, r3, topic t08); spacing from a few layout primitives instead of per-screen margins (d7, t09); one DESIGN.md per repo (r4); the roadmap page reads each item from its one home and stores no copy (o8). Live proof of the problem: q_max copied the map skill and it drifted, failing PR 969 (o6), and q_max holds a verbatim copy of a claude-settings test. Missing: the general rule for agents; shared UI components with variants (tokens are values, not components); shared test steps that a test can extend; and a check that finds copies. Proposed homes: a builder rule (search for the shared piece first; extend it with a variant; a copy needs a stated reason); a compliance-check group that reports duplicate code and vendored copies (o4); shared skills pinned, never vendored. Lands with the layout (o2), since o2 decides where each shared thing lives. Finding, Oct 26: three design skills are vendored into ios-adblock, joyous and degen (.claude/skills/impeccable, frontend-design, web-design-guidelines). The three impeccable copies already differ from each other (SOURCE.txt, reference/document.md), and claude-settings has its own skills/impeccable with a sync workflow (impeccable-sync.yml). Same failure as the q_max map skill; fold into this step's copy check.
title: One home for each shared thing; exceptions build on it, never copy it
why: Your rule, Oct 20: never duplicate and rebuild. Anything used in more than one place (a button size, a panel gap, steps 1 to 6 of a test, a skill) has one home, and everything else points at it. An exception (a different button, a twist on step 5a) calls the shared piece and changes only what differs, so a fix to the shared piece reaches every use and nothing drifts. The result looks the same; it is just more resilient.
